title: An Early Christian Basilica at 'Ein Hanniya
author: D. C. Baramki
location_note: Spring of 'Ein Hanniya, twelve kilometres south-west of Jerusalem; no map reference; placed by name. Pages 113-114 inferred from the contents (113) and the numbered leaves 115-117.
notes: Excavated June 1932: basilica with atrium, narthex, mosaic nave (vine trellis, iconoclastic damage), diakonikon and prothesis; reliquary casket in a rock-cut cavity under the altar; Umayyad coins and lamps. Church tentatively 5th-6th c., altered in the early 8th c.

features.site: outside the church, south and east sides
features.subtype: rock-cut channel from the direction of the spring, skirting the church

features.subtype: small cup-mark in the atrium floor; rock-cut cavity under the altar holding a reliquary casket
features.period: with the church, tentatively fifth or sixth century
features.quote: contained a small cup-mark at the west end of the south colonnade
